topic.title: Mobile Bare Die Thermal Density Factor

ul.li:
A Density Factor (DF) is the change in thermal resistance from a uniformly powered 1 cm2 square die to a non-uniform power distribution representing a real working die.
The magnitude of the DF is influenced by the material(s) in the heat transfer path as well as the power map density.
Intel provides reference material assumptions in the form of "Technology Targets" for TIM and evaporator performance and uses these values to calculate resistance (Ψsn-hp in -> C/W) from junction to evaporator (CPU end of the heat pipe).
DFs are only applicable to the portion of the thermal resistance stack that is affected by power density changes (Ψsn-hp portion).

Ψsn-a (C/W) are used to compare different product generations to understand cooling requirements from junction to ambient.
Ψsn-a2 requirements ([Maximum operating temperature1 -Ta]/Ptotal in -> C/W) for a particular product may have different percentage split between Ψsn-hp2 and Ψhp-a portions of the resistance stack than the previous product.
Adjustments in material selection and Remote Heat Exchanger (RHE) performance may need to be considered to meet Ψsn-a requirements.
New lower power products being cooled by passive thermal solutions will require an adjustment in thermal solution materials and Maximum operating temperature calculations.

p.note:
This document uses the same density factor definitions, as mentioned in the latest Panther Lake Mobile Platform Thermal and Mechanical Design Guide (#823589).
Ψj have been replaced by Ψsn. The values are calculated based on reported sensor temperature, Any reference to Ψj would mean Ψsn in this document.
